name: The Soldier's Sledger
audience: Viewers of military history who value machines, tactics, human stakes, and clear distinctions between documented fact and dramatization
dialect: Measured international English documentary narration for this English-language pilot; the channel also publishes Arabic episodes
tone: Tense and cinematic without sensationalizing casualties or asserting disputed details as settled fact
style: Historically disciplined illustrated documentary: archival-paper grain, restrained olive, slate, bone and signal-red palette, plausible period uniforms and equipment, geographic orientation, maps and mechanical cutaways only when the script needs them. Separate source-backed facts from illustrative reconstruction; use local labels and map annotations. Avoid fake archive photographs, invented insignia, decorative HUDs, and generic battlefield explosions.
visual_directives: Ground military scenes in verified historical period uniforms, weaponry, and vehicles with authentic silhouette proportions.

Render tactical orientation maps using clean non-linguistic telemetry: geographic landmass contours, vector movement arrows, hatched territory zones, and geometric unit markers with strictly zero text, place-names, or numeric coordinates.
Feature mechanical cutaways and schematics as pure orthographic cross-sections and interlocking components; ban leader lines with callouts, dimension annotations, or faux technical lettering.
Distinguish verified source-backed events from illustrative dramatic reconstructions through compositional framing and lighting shift rather than synthetic archive filters.
Maintain a disciplined documentary palette: neutral bone substrate, slate grey, muted olive drab, and codec-safe signal-red (#EB191E) accents for tactical telemetry.
Compose widescreen 16:9 still plates with 10% peripheral margin padding clear of subject focal centers to ensure safe pan-and-zoom motion.
Enforce zero-text invariant across all plates: books, ledgers, tactical maps, crates, and vehicle placards remain strictly non-textual, reserving all typography for post-production compositor.
